title: Getting Started Again
eyebrow: Proposal from the friction audit · one combined plan · nothing built yet
approval: Design approved: friction audit combined plan

short.lead: You asked for all of the fixes together, with Start here as a new screen beside Focus. This is that plan. Start here is added as the first screen and shows three suggested tasks. Focus stays, gets a project search, and stops showing workflow labels like Needs review. Settings gets a list where you choose which labels are kinds of work and which count as priority. Sort gets a project list you can search and a main button at the bottom. Separately, outside the app, I would list the Focus Deck GitHub issues that look finished, for you to check. Nothing is built until you approve.
short.hint: Tap each row to see its picture. Start with 'The plan', which shows how the screens connect. The rows marked 'Today' are the real app at your size. The other pictures are drawings of the plan.
items: The app opens on Start here. From there, the Start button on a suggestion goes straight to your task. 'Choose it myself' opens Focus, which works as it does today. 'Thoughts to sort' opens Sort. Board, Projects and Settings stay in the menu.
Follow the arrows from 'Open the app'.

items: Kept, and fits on one screen
The five busiest folders show, with 'Find a project' to reach the other 22. The 25 kind-of-work cards are smaller and sit in five rows, so the whole page fits on one screen instead of 2.7.

items: Choose your kinds of work and priority labels

A new Settings list. Ticked labels show on Focus. Unticked ones (Needs review, Duplicate, AjsAgent created this, and other workflow labels) stay on your tasks and on GitHub, but you never pick from them. The labels 'Asap' and 'highest priority' count as Urgent, so Start here can rank by them.
Check that the unticked labels in the picture are the ones you would untick.

items.caption: The new Settings list. A drawing, not built.

items: Each thought shows at the top. Below it is 'File to' with a search box and the projects you used most recently. The main 'File to' button and Later sit at the bottom, where your thumb is. The three steps (choose a project, add labels, link to other tasks) stay.
Check that the 'File to' button at the bottom is where your thumb reaches.

items.alt: Phone drawing of Sort: the thought, a searchable project list, and File to and Later buttons at the bottom
items.caption: Sort on a phone in the plan. A drawing, not built.

items: This is the part I called option D earlier. It changes nothing in the app. It is a clean-up of the Focus Deck issue list on GitHub. There are 97 open issues. I would list the 30 that look finished or replaced (15 built and waiting for your review, the 8 old Board issues #140 to #147, and the 7 issues named Burst A to Burst G, which only group other issues), and suggest one set of priority labels. You tick what to close. Nothing changes on GitHub until you say yes.
Answer the third question in Choices: 'Should I do the GitHub tidy-up (D)?'

It is added, not swapped in. Focus stays in the menu.
Adds 'Find a project' and hides workflow labels.
The folders, index cards and sticky note look and work as today.
A tick list of your labels, plus which labels count as priority.
Your labels on GitHub are not changed.
Project list you can search, main button at the bottom.

choices: opens
Which screen should the app open on?
Start here
You see three suggested tasks first, and Focus is one tap away.
Focus
The app opens as it does today, and Start here is the first tab.
The last screen you used
The app remembers where you were, on each device.
I suggest Start here because starting is the hardest step, and this makes it the first thing you see.
order
How should I build it?
In four parts, one at a time
Settings and labels first, then Start here, then the Focus search, then Sort. You can try each part before the next.
All in one go
One change to test, but a longer wait before you can use any of it.
I suggest four parts because each one is useful by itself and is easier for you to check.
github
Should I do the GitHub tidy-up (D)?
Yes, list the issues for me to check
You get a list of 30 issues to tick. Nothing changes on GitHub until you say yes.
Not now
The issue list stays as it is, and only the app changes.
I suggest Yes because 97 open issues make it hard to see what is actually left.

wrapup.summary: One combined plan: a new Start here screen beside Focus, a project search and fewer labels on Focus, a Settings list for your labels, faster Sort, and a separate GitHub tidy-up. My suggestions are to open on Start here, build in four parts, and do the tidy-up.
wrapup.changing: Changed: Focus, Sort, Settings and the menu, and Start here is added. Kept: Board, Projects, the jotter, your data and sync.
wrapup.blocking: Waiting on your answers to the three questions in Choices. Nothing is built until you approve.
wrapup.next: After you send your answers, I will open GitHub issues for each part and build the first one, Settings and labels. You will get a test page for each part before the next starts.
